newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria to set CA share swap ratio in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria to set CA share swap ratio in autumn.

text.p: Bank Austria, the country's top bank, said on Wednesday it would announce in the autumn the ratio at which it would swap shares of Creditanstalt, which it acquired in January.

"The final ratio will be announced this autumn at a special shareholders' meeting," chief executive Gerhard Randa told the bank's annual general meeting. The ratio was currently being evaluated by two international accounting firms.

Bank Austria in January bought the Austrian state's 70 percent voting stake in its closest domestic competitor for about 17 billion schillings in cash, creating Europe's 30th biggest banking group in terms of assets.

Under the terms of the deal, Bank Austria agreed to buy out small shareholders of Creditanstalt by offering them its own shares. They would also be offered a cash alternative of 722.5 schillings each.

Randa said auditors KPMG and Deloitte Touche were currently assessing the value of the two banks, which came under one roof in March, on the basis of their 1996 figures. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
